claims.head: Top line on top line: McDavid vs. Kakko

notes.text: The forward lines keep changing. Even their four most-used trios over the last 10 games cover only 32% of their forwards’ 5-on-5 time, the 11th-lowest in the league (a typical team: 38%). The lines listed lean on their latest games, but expect new combinations tonight.

Jared McCann is out 10 weeks (lower body injury) and has missed the last 11 games. He is one of their most valuable skaters. Kaapo Kakko has taken his spot beside Matty Beniers and Mackie Samoskevich. That line has had 77% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 48:46 together, up from 57% with McCann.

Cale Fleury has not dressed for the last 4 games. He is one of their more valuable skaters. Ryan Lindgren has taken his spot beside Josh Mahura. That pair has had 44% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 42:46 together.
Vince Dunn has started killing penalties: on the ice for 31% of the team’s shorthanded time in 22 games, up from 2% last season.
Zach Hyman is out (impaired vision injury) and has missed the last 2 games. He is a top-six forward. Connor McDavid has taken his spot beside Ryan Nugent-Hopkins and Kasperi Kapanen.
Ryan Nugent-Hopkins returned in their last game after missing 5 games. Their recent numbers were built mostly without him.
Kasperi Kapanen has started playing on the power play: on the ice for 53% of the team’s power-play time in 27 games, up from 6% last season.
Ty Emberson is no longer killing penalties: 2% of the team’s shorthanded time in 21 games, down from 30% last season.

story.head: Draisaitl’s favorite opponent
paras: The Oilers won the teams’ first meeting this season, 3-1 in Edmonton on Oct 3. The Oilers are winless in four (0-3-1), and the Kraken (11-10-1) lost 3-1 to Chicago on Wednesday. This is a Pacific Division matchup, with the Kraken sixth (24th in the NHL) and the Oilers first (third). The Pacific has been the weakest of the four divisions so far.

The Kraken’s record (.523) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.444), largely thanks to their finishing. So is the Oilers’ (.704 on chances worth .542), largely thanks to their finishing.

The Kraken rarely threaten on the penalty kill (32nd), give up a lot of shots (32nd) and ice the puck a lot (31st). On the other side, the Oilers play slow, tight games (3rd lowest). They also have one of the league’s most dangerous power plays (2nd), and that could do real damage against the Kraken’s penalty kill (30th). Edmonton has scored 3.81 goals a game, the third most in the league. The Kraken roll four lines, but the Oilers lean on their top six.

Berkly Catton (8 G / 11 A / 19 P in 22 GP) leads the Kraken in scoring, and Brandon Montour (3 G / 13 A / 16 P in 21 GP) isn’t far behind. Connor McDavid (14 G / 45 A / 59 P in 27 GP) leads the Oilers and the whole NHL in scoring, with eight goals in eleven games against Seattle since 2023-24. Leon Draisaitl (23 G / 24 A / 47 P in 27 GP) has a team-high 23 goals, tied for the most in the NHL.
Philipp Grubauer (6-5-1 / .894 SV% in 11 GS) is expected to start for Seattle, and Tristan Jarry (6-1-4 / .904 SV% in 11 GS) for Edmonton.
At home, Mike Babcock likes to send Nugent-Hopkins, McDavid and Kapanen out against the other team’s top line, so watch for them against Kakko, Beniers and Samoskevich.
